title: Leonardo
html_source: This is da Vinci, whose Mona Lisa has conventionally been associated with Dante’s Beatrice because of a passage in Dante’s Convivio in which he describes a woman’s smile, the focus of da Vinci’s masterpiece, along with her eyes, “by a beautiful simile, may be called the balconies of the lady who dwells in the architecture of the body, that is to say the soul, because she often shows herself there as if under a veil.” This mention of the “soul” bears on the nearby references to it here in Eumaeus.
